name: MEFB (Multi-Exposure Image Fusion Benchmark)
description: Multi-exposure image fusion (MEF) is an important area in computer vision and has attracted increasing interests in recent years. Apart from conventional algorithms, deep learning techniques have also been applied to multi-exposure image fusion. However, although much efforts have been made on developing MEF algorithms, the lack of benchmark makes it difficult to perform fair and comprehensive performance comparison among MEF algorithms, thus significantly hindering the development of this field. In this paper, we fill this gap by proposing a benchmark for multi-exposure image fusion (MEFB) which consists of a test set of 100 image pairs, a code library of 16 algorithms, 20 evaluation metrics, 1600 fused images and a software toolkit. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first benchmark in the field of multi-exposure image fusion. Extensive experiments have been conducted using MEFB for comprehensive performance evaluation and for identifying effective algorithms. We expect that MEFB will serve as an effective platform for researchers to compare performances and investigate MEF algorithms.
evaluation_method: objective image quality metrics (e.g., SSIM, PSNR, MI, Qabf and other specialized fusion metrics)
general_score_metric: no single primary metric — composite / per‑metric image quality scores (e.g., SSIM, MI) are reported
reputation: Presented as the first comprehensive benchmark for multi‑exposure image fusion, it is a key reference within the niche MEF research community.
notes: Small test set (100 image pairs); uses many specialized objective metrics making cross‑metric comparison nontrivial; domain‑specific (non‑LLM) benchmark and susceptible to dataset‑specific biases and metric saturation.
